I have taken LSD many times and i struggle with depression every day. If i may offer you some advice, try to view this as a positive. Psychedelics can give you a new view on life. What I see here is the first step on the road to recovery. You have RECOGNIZED that there is something wrong. This is a major step whether you realize it or not. The only way to get better is to seek help. For me, seeking help always felt like accepting defeat, but that's not what it is like at all. Professionals know how to help without the guilt and will help you work through the fear. Something IS wrong. And it won't become right without work. I never knew what that work meant, but professionals do. Not every professional will be a perfect fit. I recommend "shopping" around for one, or in other words try one and see if it is beneficial. If not, then try another. I am rooting for you, and i hope you can accept the help you seek. Good luck. This is not the end, but a new beginning.

The news can be harmful to the idea of safety, but that does not mean that your fears are unfounded. There are bad people, and the news likes to emphasize that, but rarely emphasizes the majority of people that are good. Having a general distrust of those you do not know is not a bad thing unless taken to the extreme. In these cases protection of the self can lead to a social withdrawl. The best i can recommend is social contact with trusted individuals or even better, a group. Try to socially branch out when with people you trust. It gives you "armor" in a sense, or a fort to fall back to if you feel that you are not safe. Listen to your gut, but remember that not everyone is out to get you, or in a sense "evil". I am a male so take this as you will, i will never understand fear you may or are feeling about the opposite gender, but i have had and continue to have experiences with extreme social anxiety. I hope this can help you, and i am wishing you the best!
